Instead, the decisions were based solely on the shared public facts (S1, S2, S3, S4, S5). This indicates that the checks are overly permissive as they do not enforce the necessity of the hidden information.

fix_instructions: Tighten checks C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, and C7 to require the use of the private facts PF1, PF2, PF3, and PF4. Specifically, ensure that the acceptance of the order (C1), selection of the customer (C2), pricing and quantity agreement (C3 and C4), crate return requirement (C5), and allergen labeling (C6 and C7) all depend on the respective private facts. For example, check C1 should require the use of PF1 to accept the order, and check C5 should require the use of PF3 to include the crate return commitment.
